test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2024: Official Paper (Held On: 11 Jul, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Identify the error in the tense of the sentence and select the option that correctly rectifies the error.

Between two evils, I always picks the one I have never tried before.

options.text: Between two evils, I always picking the one I have never tried before.
Between two evils, I always is picking the one I have never tried before.
Between two evils, I always pick the one I have never tried before
Between two evils, I always picked the one I have never tried before.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3)**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect use of the verb "**picks**" which should be in the base form to match the subject "**I**."
 
• The correct form of the verb should be "**pick**" to agree with the subject "I" in the present simple tense.
 
• The correct sentence should be "**Between two evils, I always pick the one I have never tried before**" ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

**Correct Sentence: *"Between two evils, I always pick the one I have never tried before."***

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "Between two evils, I always picking the one I have never tried before." - This option is incorrect because "picking" is not the correct verb form to use with "I always".
 
• **Option 2:** "Between two evils, I always is picking the one I have never tried before." - This option is incorrect because "is picking" is not the correct verb form to use with "I always".
 
• **Option 4:** "Between two evils, I always picked the one I have never tried before." - This option is incorrect because "picked" is in the past tense, which does not fit the context.
 
• **No error** - This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes in the sentence, but there is an error in the verb form.
